questions.prompt: Assess this claim: The KV cache stores only model weights.
questions.referenceAnswer:
Answer: False

A decoder predicts the next token under a causal mask. RoPE encodes relative position through rotations; RMSNorm rescales activations and SwiGLU gates feed-forward features. MQA shares one key/value head and GQA shares them within groups, reducing KV-cache memory. The cache stores previous keys and values during decoding.

questions.prompt: Assess this claim: A tokenizer maps text into a vocabulary of token IDs.
questions.referenceAnswer:
Answer: True

A tokenizer maps text into a vocabulary of token IDs. Pretraining minimizes next-token cross entropy over large text corpora. Deduplication, quality filtering and held-out contamination checks are part of the data pipeline. Compute/data scaling tradeoffs compare parameter count and training tokens under a fixed budget, rather than assuming larger is always better.
keyPoints: A tokenizer maps text into a vocabulary of token IDs.
Pretraining minimizes next-token cross entropy over large text corpora.
Deduplication, quality filtering and held-out contamination checks are part of the data pipeline.

questions.prompt:
The prefix 'The capital is' supports many continuations depending on the preceding context; a fluent continuation can still be false.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
A language model assigns a distribution to the next token conditional on a prefix. Training compares that distribution with the observed continuation. This objective can teach useful patterns without directly guaranteeing truth, reasoning skill, or calibrated confidence.

The model estimates a conditional token distribution rather than consulting a guaranteed fact table.
keyPoints: The model estimates a conditional token distribution rather than consulting a guaranteed fact table.
A language model assigns a distribution to the next token conditional on a prefix.

questions.prompt:
For tokens [A, B, C], inputs [A, B] predict targets [B, C]. Allowing A to attend to B leaks its target.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Decoder training predicts every next token in parallel while a causal mask prevents each position from seeing future input tokens. Targets are shifted relative to inputs. Padding and special-token positions need an explicit loss policy.

Shift targets and block future-token attention to preserve the prediction task.
keyPoints: Shift targets and block future-token attention to preserve the prediction task.
Decoder training predicts every next token in parallel while a causal mask prevents each position from seeing future input tokens.

questions.prompt:
A common word may be one token while an unusual identifier becomes several pieces.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Byte-pair encoding builds larger token units through merge rules. Runtime tokenization applies a fixed vocabulary and merge procedure; it does not retrain on each input. The resulting token boundaries affect sequence length, rare strings, and multilingual efficiency.

A deployed tokenizer applies its existing vocabulary and merge rules.
keyPoints: A deployed tokenizer applies its existing vocabulary and merge rules.
Byte-pair encoding builds larger token units through merge rules.

questions.prompt:
A tokenizer that normalizes whitespace differently can change the token sequence seen by a checkpoint.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
WordPiece describes a subword modeling approach, while SentencePiece is a tokenizer toolkit supporting approaches such as unigram and BPE. Tokenizer normalization and whitespace handling are part of the model interface. Tokenizers are not interchangeable simply because vocabulary sizes match.

Match the full tokenizer configuration to the checkpoint.
keyPoints: Match the full tokenizer configuration to the checkpoint.
WordPiece describes a subword modeling approach, while SentencePiece is a tokenizer toolkit supporting approaches such as unigram and BPE.

questions.prompt:
A residual block returns an input plus a transformed branch; normalization may occur before the branch computation.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
RMSNorm rescales activations using their root mean square rather than subtracting a feature mean as LayerNorm does. Residual pathways preserve an additive route through a block. Placement and numerical precision affect optimization, so normalization is an architectural choice rather than a cosmetic replacement.

RMSNorm and LayerNorm use different normalization statistics.
keyPoints: RMSNorm and LayerNorm use different normalization statistics.
RMSNorm rescales activations using their root mean square rather than subtracting a feature mean as LayerNorm does.

questions.prompt:
The same content at two positions receives different rotated queries and keys.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
RoPE applies position-dependent rotations to query and key components. Their dot products then encode relative positional relationships. Extending context through scaling changes how positions are represented and needs evaluation beyond simply changing a maximum-length setting.

Context-extension changes require long-context quality evaluation.
keyPoints: Context-extension changes require long-context quality evaluation.
RoPE applies position-dependent rotations to query and key components.

questions.prompt:
Repeated low-quality pages can dominate a mixture even if the total corpus appears diverse.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
A training corpus needs documented provenance, usage constraints, quality rules, and representation goals. Mixture weights determine which sources influence training. A large token count does not compensate for mislabeled, contaminated, or systematically biased data.

Track source quality and mixture composition alongside total tokens.
keyPoints: Track source quality and mixture composition alongside total tokens.
A training corpus needs documented provenance, usage constraints, quality rules, and representation goals.

questions.prompt:
A benchmark solution reproduced with minor punctuation changes may evade an exact-hash check.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Deduplication reduces repeated examples and near-duplicate leakage. Contamination checks compare evaluation material with training sources using more than exact string equality. The detection method can miss paraphrases or shared templates, so document its limits.

Use layered contamination checks and report what they cannot detect.
keyPoints: Use layered contamination checks and report what they cannot detect.
Deduplication reduces repeated examples and near-duplicate leakage.

questions.prompt:
Training on malformed assistant turns can teach the model to reproduce formatting errors.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
SFT trains on curated instruction-response examples. The loss mask defines which tokens contribute: some recipes supervise assistant responses while treating instructions as context. Data quality, coverage, and formatting determine behavior more directly than the label 'instruction data'.

Define supervision and formatting explicitly for the intended assistant behavior.
keyPoints: Define supervision and formatting explicitly for the intended assistant behavior.
SFT trains on curated instruction-response examples.

questions.prompt:
A reward model may prefer longer answers even when they add unsupported claims.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Preference data compares alternatives under a specified rubric. A reward model approximates these judgments and can exploit superficial correlations. Evaluate agreement across annotators, distribution shifts, and adversarial responses before treating its score as a reliable objective.

Reward scores are learned proxies that require independent validation.
keyPoints: Reward scores are learned proxies that require independent validation.
Preference data compares alternatives under a specified rubric.

questions.prompt:
A model with many total expert parameters may execute only a subset per token while still needing storage for all experts.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Dense layers activate their parameters for each token; MoE routes tokens to a subset of expert networks. Active compute and total stored parameters are different quantities. Routing balance, expert communication, and capacity policies influence real performance.

MoE can reduce active compute without reducing total parameter storage proportionally.
keyPoints: MoE can reduce active compute without reducing total parameter storage proportionally.
Dense layers activate their parameters for each token; MoE routes tokens to a subset of expert networks.

questions.prompt:
A fact outside a local window may need a global-attention pathway to influence a later prediction.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Windowed attention limits which prior tokens some layers can access. This changes attention and cache requirements but may affect tasks needing distant evidence. Mixed local/global architectures require layer-specific accounting rather than one universal full-context cache formula.

Cache accounting must reflect the attention policy of each layer.
keyPoints: Cache accounting must reflect the attention policy of each layer.
Windowed attention limits which prior tokens some layers can access.
